scenario: AITA For telling my Girlfriend she needs to quit whining about who eats what or I'll kick her out | Well, the title says it all, the past few weeks have both been really great and extremely infuriating. We don't live together, but we decided it would be best to stick together during these times as we have no family near as such she is staying with me as I have my own apartment and she has multiple roommates hence the choice. Well she eats more then any person I have ever known, especially considering her physical appearance, she is 5'4, petite, thin and yet she eats more than I do and I am 6'6 and a bit of a gymbro. To put it in to perspective, our food bill each week is roughly three times compared to what I usually spend alone. Yet she seems extremely selfconcious about this and as a result will act surprised when something is gone, try to blame me, states I am eating too much whenever I eat anything, essentially, she tries to deflect her eating habits and projects them on to me out of embarrassment about her eating so much I guess? The thing is, I don't care about her eating habits, she can eat whatever she wants to eat what I am done with is her constantly trying to blame me, whining about food and picking fights about it. I talked to her about it multiple times, argued with her about it multiple times but earlier today I just got so tired of another comment, this time brought on by me making a sandwhich at 2 PM when I had eaten at 10 AM I know right, horrible. So I told her that this crap was either going to stop right here and now or I'll kick her out and she can spend the coming weeks or months at her own place. She just started crying, called me horrible and locked herself in the bathroom. At this point I just dont get it anymore, am I being TA here or is she TA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is being "AITA" (Am I The Asshole) or not. Let me break it down step by step. First, the situation: The person is living with their girlfriend during tough times because they don't have family nearby. The girlfriend has multiple roommates, so staying with him makes sense. However, she eats a lot more than him, even though she's petite and thin, while he's 6'6 and into the gym. Their weekly food bill has tripled because of her eating habits. He's frustrated because she's constantly whining about the food, blaming him for eating too much, and acting surprised when things run out. He's tried talking to her multiple times, but it keeps happening. Finally, he snapped and told her she needs to stop or he'll kick her out. She cried, called him horrible, and locked herself in the bathroom. So, is he the asshole here? Let's consider both sides. On one hand, he's accommodating her by letting her stay with him when she has roommates. That's kind and considerate. However, her eating habits are causing a significant increase in their expenses, which is understandable to be frustrated about. He's tried to communicate his feelings, but she's not changing her behavior. The constant whining and blame-shifting are making the situation worse. On the other hand, he's reacting by threatening to kick her out, which might be a bit harsh. While it's okay to set boundaries, the way he delivered the message could be seen as insensitive, especially since she's already feeling self-conscious about her eating. His threat might have come across as more about control or anger rather than a constructive solution. I think the key points are communication and boundaries. He's right to feel frustrated and to address the issue, but the way he handled it might have been too confrontational. Maybe there's a better way to discuss the problem without making her feel attacked. However, he's also not wrong to want peace and a stress-free living situation. In the end, while his intentions might be good, the method he used could be seen as a bit harsh, making him the asshole in this situation. But it's a close call because he's dealing with a tough issue that's affecting his life as well.
